topic: Research: JetBrains Research: Understanding AI's Real Impact on Developer Workflows (2026)

key_points: AI adoption keeps climbing to 80% of developers, but trust in AI output is weakening.
Almost-right AI code is a major pain point: 45% cite it as their top frustration and 66% spend more time fixing such code.
Only 23% of developers still rely on vibe coding in professional work, showing adoption is still task-centric.
Organizations lose about 7 hours per team member weekly to AI-related inefficiencies.
85% of respondents say platform engineering is essential for AI-driven productivity, while 60% use more than five dev tools and 49% use more than five AI tools.
AI is near-universal among software teams: 90% adoption and median 2 hours/day usage.
Over 80% of professionals report productivity improvements and 59% report improved code quality, but trust remains mixed with only 24%+20% reporting high trust.
GitHub activity remains at scale: more than 36 million developers joined in one year and over 180 million developers now work and build on GitHub.
The report frames AI, agents, and typed-language adoption as central workflow shifts for the ecosystem.
Top-performing AI-driven software organizations report 16-30% gains in productivity/time-to-market and 31-45% gains in software quality.
McKinsey reports AI coding benchmark scores nearly doubled in one year (30→55), but organizations need operating-model change to fully realize gains.

stats.fact: Google DORA: 90% of software development professionals now use AI, up 14% YoY; 65% rely heavily on it.
Google DORA: Over 80% of professionals report AI increases productivity; 59% say code quality improved.
GitLab: Organizations lose 7 hours/week/team member to AI-related inefficiencies and 85% say platform engineering is essential.
Stack Overflow: 80% of developers use AI in workflows; 66% spend more time fixing near-correct AI code.
JetBrains AI Pulse (Jan 2026): 90% of developers used at least one AI tool at work; 74% adopted specialized AI coding tools/agents.
GitHub Octoverse: GitHub saw over 36 million new developers in one year and now supports 180 million-plus developers.
GitHub Octoverse: The developer flow report highlights over 986 million code pushes in 2025, indicating continued cadence growth at scale.

angles: AI productivity gains are real, but validation and debug overhead are becoming the bottleneck for net throughput.
Near-universal adoption masks low confidence—teams still need strong review loops and quality governance.
Language/tool selection is increasingly an AI-compatibility strategy, not only a developer preference.
The biggest gains now come from platform-level workflow design, not point AI feature adoption.
Organizational operating model shifts (roles, governance, and delivery cadence) determine whether AI is a multiplier or a friction source.
